subject: Run-rate commitment window + peak TPS qualification — NovaCorp hosted API pricing
messages:
From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
To: Elena Park <elena@novacorp.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Run-rate commitment window + peak TPS qualification — NovaCorp hosted API pricing

Hi Elena — great to meet earlier.

Quick recap from our discovery call and the pricing/ops points we covered:

- Expected steady-state monthly token volume: 12–18M tokens (mostly 2–3k token prompts; average response ~380 tokens).
- Launch-day / marketing spikes: short bursts to ~200–240 TPS for 8–20 minutes; expected <8 days/month with spikes. Sustained 99th-percentile TPS outside spikes: ~120–160 TPS.
- Preferred budget band you mentioned: target $18–22 / 1M tokens (net of discounts for committed slab).
- Key sensitivities: concurrency throttles on short-lived spikes, and caching opportunities on prefix prompts that could reduce billable tokens by ~10–15%.

Next steps I promised on the call:
1) I’ll share an initial mutual action plan (MAP) with slab pricing options and a burst policy (attached).
2) Karthik will model the unit economics for the 12/15/18M scenarios and include a projected monthly spend table.
3) Marissa to coordinate a procurement intro and share standard SOW/SLA templates.

I attached the MAP draft and a snapshot of the pricing bands. If the $/1M target is firm at $20, we’ll look at a 12–18 month slab with incremental discounts at 50M and 120M annualized commitments (we outlined ranges on the attachment).

Can you confirm 1) the nominal run-rate you expect to sign for the first 3 months, and 2) whether NovaCorp requires on-premise logs or a strict VPC-only setup for the pilot? That affects the Dedicated vs Hosted decision and the SLA language.

Thanks — talk soon.

— Markus Klein
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Attachments: NovaCorp_MAP_v1.xlsx; Redwood_pricing_bands_v3.pdf

From: Elena Park <elena@novacorp.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Cc: procure@novacorp.com, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 11:07:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Run-rate commitment window + peak TPS qualification — NovaCorp hosted API pricing

Thanks Markus — helpful summary.

Quick clarifications from our side:
- We’re comfortable projecting an initial billing run-rate of ~15M tokens/mo for Q1 post-launch. Launch marketing days could push API calls to the 200–230 TPS range for short windows (10–15 mins), maybe 5–7 days in the quarter rather than the month — apologies for the back-and-forth on cadence.
- Budget guidance: procurement has a target of $20 / 1M tokens (gross) as the ceiling for the pilot. If you can map net effective price after standard credits, that helps our internal math.
- We do not need an on-prem data path for the pilot but will require restricted retention (30 days) and audit logs for the pilot phase. Procurement will likely request the SLA and SOC2 evidence before sign.

procure@novacorp.com will start the baseline paperwork; they’ll need a short MAP and a redlineable SOW.

On the spike behavior: can you confirm whether Redwood supports automatic short-term burst capacity above the committed slab, and what the overage rate would look like if we exceed the burst allowance on a given day? Also please confirm the 99th-percentile TPS measurement window you use (1m / 5m / 15m).

Thanks,

Elena Park
Head of Product — NovaCorp

From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 14:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Run-rate commitment window + peak TPS qualification — NovaCorp hosted API pricing

Elena — thanks for the clarifications. Quick answers and a proposed plan:

- Burst capacity: yes — Redwood supports automatic short-term burst above committed slabs via our burst pool. For the hosted API pilot we can allow up to 250 TPS for 15 minutes/day without penalizing the slab, then bill overages at a pre-agreed overage tier. Draft overage tiers are in the attached pricing PDF (we typically ladder: 1.5x list for ad-hoc bursts, 1.1x for scheduled burst windows under a managed plan).
- 99th-percentile TPS measurement: we report 1-minute windows by default and provide 5m and 15m aggregates on the console; SLA adherence uses the 1-minute 99th metric.
- Retention/audit logs: 30-day retention is fine for the pilot; we’ll include the SOC2 artifact and a short SSO/KMS note in the SOW (attached SLA_Draft.pdf).

Action items (who/what/when):
- Markus: update MAP to include a 15M tier example at $20 / 1M (net scenario) + burst allowance rows — delivery EOD Thu (11/19).
- Karthik: run unit-econ table (12/15/18M) with CPU/GPU cost assumptions and expected net margin for Redwood — delivery Mon (11/23).
- Marissa: intro to our contracts lead and attach the redlineable SOW + SOC2 link — delivery Mon (11/23).
- Elena / Procurement: confirm nominal Q1 commit (15M) and any required procurement terms — please aim for Fri (11/20).

If that timeline works I’ll set up a brief 30-minute follow-up on Tue (11/24) to walk the MAP and pricing bands.

Thanks — Markus
